passage: At the corner of the Seoul schoolyard, Leila lowered her voice. "Come on, tell us what Yuna said about her grandmother's cooking. Everyone's laughing." Soo-ah's palms turned damp. If she said nothing, they might start whispering about her next. She had seen it happen to Mina last month. "I don't really have anything," she said, and smiled politely. Leila's eyes narrowed. "Boring." Soo-ah's heart thudded as she picked up her bag. "See you in class, Leila." Walking away, she felt shaky. In the library she noticed Hana, who always saved a seat for her without asking for anything. She sat down beside her.

qa.q: What did Leila want Soo-ah to tell them about?
qa.a: What Yuna said about her grandmother's cooking.

qa.q: What was Soo-ah afraid of when her palms turned damp?
qa.a: That if she said nothing, they might start whispering about her next, as she had seen happen to Mina.

qa.q: What would you advise Soo-ah about her friendship with Leila?
qa.a: Stay polite and out of the gossip, and spend time with kinder friends like Hana, since a friend who needs cruelty is not safe. 🙂

qa.q: How might Hana see Soo-ah's choice?
qa.a: Hana asks nothing of Soo-ah and saves her a seat, so she probably welcomes her and sees a friend who doesn't need gossip.

grounding: A child fears being gossiped about if she refuses to gossip, stays polite and out of it, and moves toward a kinder friend.

passage:
I'm Zainab. In Class 6, the girls I sat with loved gossip. One day they started on Chaitanya, the quiet boy who ate lunch alone. "He smells like onions." "He's so weird."
I didn't join in. But I was scared. What would they say about me if I didn't laugh?
So sometimes I laughed a little. And every time I felt worse.
Then one day I heard them whispering about me after I left the table. That was when I understood: a group that needs cruelty isn't safe for anyone.
I stayed polite, but I stopped sitting with them. I started eating with the chess club kids. Chaitanya was one of them.

qa.q: What did the girls say Chaitanya smelled like?

qa.a: Zainab feared that without laughing along, Zainab would become the group's next target.

qa.q: What did Zainab do once the fear came true?
qa.a: Zainab stayed polite but stopped sitting with the gossiping group and found kinder friends at the chess club.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt eating lunch alone?
qa.a: Chaitanya may have felt lonely and left out, especially if he sensed people talking about him.

grounding: Zainab fears being gossiped about if not joining in, sees a group that needs cruelty is not safe, and moves to kinder friends.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Wednesday.
Elizabeth has been sitting with a group of girls who talk about others constantly. I've noticed she laughs nervously but doesn't join in, and she looks uncomfortable.
Today she stayed back. She said, "If I don't gossip with them, they'll gossip about me. They already did to Neha when she left."
I told her that a group that needs cruelty to stay together isn't really safe. She can stay polite without joining.
This afternoon, I saw her sitting with Gautam and his friends from the gardening club, laughing properly for the first time in weeks.

qa.q: Which club are Gautam and his friends from?

qa.a: She feared the group would gossip about her if she didn't join in, as they had about Neha.

qa.q: What advice did the teacher give Elizabeth?
qa.a: That a group that needs cruelty isn't safe, and she can stay polite without joining.

qa.q: How might Gautam and his friends see Elizabeth joining them?
qa.a: They seem to welcome her, since she is laughing with them properly.

grounding: A girl fears being gossiped about if she stops joining in; a teacher explains such a group is not safe, and she finds kinder friends.
